title: Mock 7 · Tough Simulator B
blurb: Exam-day difficulty: multi-statement items, nuanced rules and two caselets.

questions.q: Which of the following is a LIMITATION of alternative investments listed in the workbook?
options: They do not satisfy the requirement for regular income
They help diversify risk beyond traditional avenues
They give access to experienced managers
They provide growth capital to companies that cannot easily raise bank finance
questions.explanation: Table 1.2 lists limitations including complex structuring, tedious documentation, less transparency, illiquidity and not satisfying the need for regular income.
hints: Correct: listed among limitations.
Wrong: a benefit.
Wrong: a benefit.
Wrong: a benefit.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a 'special situation asset' for a Special Situation Fund?
options: Security receipts issued by an RBI-registered ARC
Stressed loans available for acquisition under RBI's Master Direction
Shares of a company whose loan default has continued for only 30 days
Securities of a company whose borrowings are under the corporate insolvency resolution process
questions.explanation: Securities of companies with disclosed defaults qualify only if the payment default continues for at least ninety calendar days after the default.
hints: Wrong choice: ARC security receipts qualify.
Wrong choice: stressed loans under RBI directions qualify.
Correct (not an SSA): the default must continue for at least 90 calendar days.
Wrong choice: companies under CIRP qualify.

questions.q: A scheme closes with a corpus of ₹160 crore. What is the minimum continuing interest of the manager/sponsor, and can it be met by waiving 2 years of management fees worth the same amount?
options: ₹4 crore; yes, fee waiver is acceptable
₹5 crore; no, fee waiver does not count
₹4 crore; no, fee waiver does not count
₹0.8 crore; yes, fee waiver is acceptable
questions.explanation: Continuing interest is the lower of 2.5% of corpus (₹4 crore) or ₹5 crore, in the form of investment, not through waiver of management fees.
hints: Wrong: fee waiver is expressly not allowed.
Wrong: ₹5 crore is the cap, but the lower amount applies here.
Correct: 2.5% × 160 = ₹4 crore (below ₹5 crore); must be an investment, not a fee waiver.
Wrong: arithmetic and rule both wrong.

questions.q: The initial drawdown made after the first close of a fund usually provides for all of the following EXCEPT:
options: Carried interest payable to the manager
Management fees retrospective to the first close
Organisational and other expenses of the fund
Capital for investments already made before the drawdown
questions.explanation: The initial drawdown usually provides for management fees retrospective to first close, organisational expenses and capital for investments made prior to the drawdown.
hints: Correct: carry is paid only from realised returns, not drawdowns.
Wrong choice: included in initial drawdown.
Wrong choice: included in initial drawdown.
Wrong choice: included in initial drawdown.

questions.q: An investor was accredited when she joined an AI-only scheme but her net worth later fell below the threshold. What is her status in that scheme?
options: She must exit the scheme immediately
She must top up to ₹1 crore within 30 days
She continues to be reckoned as an AI for the life of the scheme
Her units are converted into a non-AI class
questions.explanation: If an investor is an AI at the time of onboarding into an AIF scheme, he/she shall be reckoned as an AI through the life of the scheme, even if the status is lost in the interim.
hints: Wrong: no forced exit.
Wrong: no such rule.
Correct: AI status at onboarding holds through the scheme's life.
Wrong: no such rule.

questions.q: Consider: (i) Category II AIFs may buy or sell credit default swaps. (ii) A Category I AIF must keep a 30-day cooling-off period between two borrowings, counted from repayment. (iii) Category II AIFs invest primarily in unlisted securities and/or listed debt rated 'A' or below. Which are correct?
options: (i), (ii) and (iii)
(i) and (ii) only
(ii) and (iii) only
(i) and (iii) only
questions.explanation: Cat II may buy or sell CDS; Cat I and II keep a 30-day cooling off from repayment of the previous borrowing; Cat II invests primarily in unlisted securities and/or listed debt rated A or below.
hints: Correct: all three statements are in the workbook.
Wrong: (iii) is also correct.
Wrong: (i) is also correct.
Wrong: (ii) is also correct.

questions.q: Why does the workbook say most Indian AIFs choose a trust rather than an LLP, with respect to the manager's liability?
options: In a trust the manager has unlimited liability
LLPs do not permit appointment of a manager
A trust allows ring-fencing of the manager's liability since the manager is only a counterparty service provider
Trusts are exempt from SEBI registration
questions.explanation: A trust structure permits ring-fencing of the manager's liability from that of the AIF because the manager is only a counterparty service provider, unlike a director or designated partner.
hints: Wrong: the opposite.
Wrong: LLPs can appoint managers through an IMA.
Correct: the manager is not on the board or a designated partner of the AIF.
Wrong: all AIFs must register.

questions.q: From GAAR's perspective, which feature of an AIF structure is MOST likely to attract scrutiny?
options: A domestic trust with only resident investors
A unified structure with genuine offshore investors and full disclosures
Appointment of a SEBI-registered custodian
A layered structure whose main purpose is a tax benefit and which lacks commercial substance
questions.explanation: Complicated structures are likely to be scrutinised under GAAR, which allows authorities to re-characterise transactions lacking commercial substance.
hints: Wrong: simple domestic structure.
Wrong: genuine purpose with disclosure.
Wrong: a regulatory requirement.
Correct: GAAR targets arrangements lacking commercial substance with tax benefit as the main purpose.

questions.q: An investment of ₹100 returns a single payment of ₹172.80 at the end of 3 years. Its IRR is:
questions.explanation: IRR solves 100 = 172.8 ÷ (1 + r)³, giving r = 20%; the holding-period ROI of 72.8% ignores time value.
hints: Wrong: that is the simple average (72.8 ÷ 3).
Wrong: too low.
Wrong: that is the absolute holding-period return.

questions.q: Which statement about the behaviour of DPI, RVPI and TVPI over a fund's life is INCORRECT?
options: During vintage years most of the fund's value is captured in DPI
Before investing, TVPI is below 1 because fees and expenses reduce the corpus
As harvesting begins, DPI rises
At complete exit, RVPI becomes zero
questions.explanation: During vintage years and growth cycles the fund's value is largely captured in unrealised value (RVPI); DPI rises only as the fund harvests investments.
hints: Correct (the incorrect statement): in vintage years value sits mainly in RVPI.
Wrong choice: this is correct.
Wrong choice: this is correct.
Wrong choice: this is correct.

questions.q: In the workbook's Alpha Fund case, the gross FIRR was 25.45%, net FIRR 24.56% and investor FIRR 20.13%. The main reason investor FIRR is lower than net FIRR is:
options: Management fees and fund expenses
Catch-up and carried interest paid to the manager under the waterfall
Taxes withheld at 30%
Currency depreciation
questions.explanation: Net FIRR already deducts fees and expenses; investor-level FIRR is lower still because final distributions follow the carry arrangement (catch-up 1,345 and carry 807).
hints: Wrong: fees and expenses explain gross versus net.
Correct: the gap between net fund IRR and investor IRR reflects carry and catch-up.
Wrong: the case ignores taxes.
Wrong: no currency element in the case.

questions.q: Which of the following statements about due diligence review (DDR) of an investee company is correct?
options: DDR is completed before the teaser is received
DDR commences only after the term sheet is executed, and the DDR report is generally not shared with the company
The DDR report is a public document filed with SEBI
The investee's statutory auditor conducts the legal DDR
questions.explanation: The due diligence process does not commence unless the term sheet is executed; a copy of the DDR report is generally not made available to the company.
hints: Wrong: the teaser comes first.
Correct: both facts are stated in the workbook.
Wrong: DDR reports are confidential.
Wrong: legal DDR is done by a law firm.

questions.q: An investor wishes to buy promoter shares before they are offered to an outsider. The right that obliges a selling shareholder to first offer shares to existing holders is:
options: Drag-along right
Liquidation preference
Affirmative right
Right of First Refusal / Right of First Offer
questions.explanation: Under ROFR/ROFO, a shareholder wishing to dispose of shares must first offer them to shareholders having the benefit of the right, before selling to third parties.
hints: Wrong: forces others to sell.
Wrong: priority on liquidation proceeds.
Wrong: consent right over corporate actions.
Correct: ROFR/ROFO operate inter-se between shareholders.

questions.q: A distributor's client is a newly-wealthy entrepreneur who needs liquidity in 2 years and has low risk appetite. The distributor recommends a 10-year early-stage VC fund because it pays the highest commission. This is:
options: Acceptable if the PPM is shared
Acceptable because AIFs are for HNIs
Acceptable if the investor signs a waiver
Commission-driven mis-selling and a breach of suitability
questions.explanation: Distributors must map investor objectives, tenure and liquidity needs to the fund; recommending schemes solely for higher commissions is a malpractice.
hints: Wrong: sharing the PPM does not cure unsuitability.
Wrong: wealth alone does not establish suitability.
Wrong: waivers do not justify mis-selling.
Correct: product does not fit the risk profile and the motive is commission.

questions.q: As per the workbook, the distributor's understanding of an investor rests on three criteria. Which of the following is NOT one of them?
options: Risk profile and investment requirements of the investor
Fund structure and governance aspects
Profile and performance track record of the investment manager
Expected distribution commission
questions.explanation: The three criteria are (1) the investor's risk profile and requirements, (2) fund structure and governance and (3) the manager's profile and track record.
hints: Wrong choice: criterion (1).
Wrong choice: criterion (2).
Wrong choice: criterion (3).
Correct: commission is not a criterion.

questions.q: Which statement about using past performance in AIF marketing material is correct?
options: Where past performance is mentioned, the benchmarking agency's performance-versus-benchmark report must also be provided
Past performance may never be mentioned in a PPM
Only gross IRR may be shown, without any benchmark
Past performance may be shown only for Category III AIFs
questions.explanation: In the PPM and any marketing material where past performance is mentioned, the performance versus benchmark report from the benchmarking agencies shall also be provided.
hints: Correct: SEBI requires the benchmark report alongside past performance.
Wrong: the PPM includes a track record section.
Wrong: the benchmark comparison is mandatory.
Wrong: applies to Cat I/II too.

questions.q: For Category I and II AIFs, benchmarking agencies construct benchmarks by vintage year mainly to:
options: Rank funds by the size of management fees
Compare funds with similar first-close timelines on a uniform basis
Calculate tax liability of investors
Replace independent valuation
questions.explanation: Benchmarks based on vintage years bring uniformity in comparison of funds with similar first close timelines, using pooled IRR, DPI, RVPI and TVPI.
hints: Wrong: not the purpose.
Correct: vintage-based benchmarks bring uniformity across funds with similar first close.
Wrong: not a tax tool.
Wrong: valuation is still required.

questions.q: A regular (non-AI, non-LVF) AIF files its first scheme's PPM on Day 0 but receives SEBI registration only on working day 15. From when can it launch the first scheme?
options: From working day 15, the date of registration
From working day 10 after filing
Immediately on Day 0
From working day 30 after filing
questions.explanation: First schemes can be launched from the date of grant of SEBI registration or after 10 working days of filing, whichever is later.
hints: Correct: later of registration date or 10 working days after filing.
Wrong: registration was not yet granted.
Wrong: only AI-only funds/LVFs launch on filing (after registration).
Wrong: 30 days was the old timeline.

questions.q: Changes in the terms of the PPM of a Category I/II AIF must be intimated to investors and SEBI:
options: On a consolidated basis within 1 month of the end of each financial year
Within 7 days of each change
Only at the time of winding up
Within 6 months of each quarter
questions.explanation: All changes in terms of the PPM and fund documents shall be intimated to investors and SEBI on a consolidated basis within 1 month of the end of each financial year.
hints: Correct: consolidated intimation within 1 month of FY end.
Wrong: not prescribed.
Wrong: too late.
Wrong: not prescribed.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a ground for winding up an AIF under Regulation 29?
options: Expiry of the tenure of the AIF or all its schemes
A resolution passed by 51% of investors by value
Trustees' opinion that winding up is in investors' interest
SEBI directing so in the interest of investors
questions.explanation: An AIF shall be wound up when tenure is over, trustees so opine, 75% of investors by value pass a resolution, or SEBI so directs.
hints: Wrong choice: a valid ground.
Correct (not a ground): the resolution threshold is 75% of investors by value.
Wrong choice: a valid ground.
Wrong choice: a valid ground.

questions.q: An AIF distributes ₹10 lakh of dividend income to a non-resident investor who has not obtained any lower-deduction certificate. The tax to be withheld is:
options: Nil, as dividends pass through
questions.explanation: For non-resident investors, tax is deducted at 20% if the income distributed is dividend; other income at rates in force or DTAA rates.
hints: Wrong: 10% applies to residents.
Wrong: pass-through does not remove withholding.
Wrong: not the prescribed rate.
Correct: 20% on dividend income to non-residents.

questions.q: Which of the following is the BEST description of a 'soft dollar arrangement' that distributors should abstain from?
options: Paying commissions in foreign currency
Offering investors a discount on management fees via a side letter
The AIF using clients' money to pay for third-party or proprietary research that benefits the manager
Paying the custodian a fixed annual fee
questions.explanation: In a soft dollar arrangement the AIF may use clients' money to pay for third-party and proprietary research; it can indirectly add to investor costs and is a conflict.
hints: Wrong: unrelated.
Wrong: a side-letter term, not soft dollars.
Correct: such arrangements indirectly raise costs borne by investors.
Wrong: ordinary service fee.

questions.q: Based on the case, can Udaan declare its first close next week?
options: No, it must on-board at least 5 accredited investors before declaring first close
Yes, 4 accredited investors are sufficient
Yes, as long as each invests ₹1 crore
No, it must first raise a corpus of ₹20 crore
questions.explanation: An Angel Fund shall on-board at least 5 accredited investors before declaring its first close; no minimum investment value applies to angel investors.
hints: Correct: minimum of five accredited investors.
Wrong: four is one short.
Wrong: no minimum investment applies to angel investors.
Wrong: the requirement cited is the number of AIs.
questions.case: Udaan Angel Fund was recently registered with SEBI as an Angel Fund. So far it has on-boarded 4 accredited investors and wants to declare its first close next week. Its manager is evaluating three proposals: (a) investing ₹30 crore in FinBuddy, a fintech start-up; (b) investing ₹2 crore in GreenLeaf, a start-up promoted by a corporate group with group turnover of ₹450 crore; and (c) selling its stake in an existing investee to an unrelated third-party buyer 7 months after the investment was made.

questions.q: What about proposal (a), investing ₹30 crore in FinBuddy?
options: Permitted, as there is no upper limit
Permitted if approved by two-thirds of investors
Not permitted, as the maximum is ₹10 lakh
Not permitted, as an angel fund's investment in an investee cannot exceed ₹25 crore
questions.explanation: Investment by an angel fund in any investee company shall not be less than ₹10 lakh and shall not exceed ₹25 crore (including follow-ons).
hints: Wrong: an upper limit exists.
Wrong: no approval overrides this limit.
Wrong: ₹10 lakh is the minimum, not maximum.
Correct: the band is ₹10 lakh to ₹25 crore.
questions.case: Udaan Angel Fund was recently registered with SEBI as an Angel Fund. So far it has on-boarded 4 accredited investors and wants to declare its first close next week. Its manager is evaluating three proposals: (a) investing ₹30 crore in FinBuddy, a fintech start-up; (b) investing ₹2 crore in GreenLeaf, a start-up promoted by a corporate group with group turnover of ₹450 crore; and (c) selling its stake in an existing investee to an unrelated third-party buyer 7 months after the investment was made.

questions.q: What about proposal (b), GreenLeaf, promoted by a corporate group with turnover of ₹450 crore?
options: Eligible, since the investment of ₹2 crore is within limits
Eligible, since group turnover is irrelevant
Not eligible, as angel funds may invest only in start-ups not related to a group whose turnover exceeds ₹300 crore
Not eligible, since the minimum investment is ₹5 crore
questions.explanation: Angel funds shall invest in start-ups not promoted, sponsored by or related to a corporate group whose group turnover exceeds ₹300 crore.
hints: Wrong: ticket size does not cure ineligibility.
Wrong: group turnover is a criterion.
Correct: the ₹300 crore group-turnover test fails.
Wrong: minimum is ₹10 lakh.
questions.case: Udaan Angel Fund was recently registered with SEBI as an Angel Fund. So far it has on-boarded 4 accredited investors and wants to declare its first close next week. Its manager is evaluating three proposals: (a) investing ₹30 crore in FinBuddy, a fintech start-up; (b) investing ₹2 crore in GreenLeaf, a start-up promoted by a corporate group with group turnover of ₹450 crore; and (c) selling its stake in an existing investee to an unrelated third-party buyer 7 months after the investment was made.

questions.q: What about proposal (c), selling to an unrelated third party 7 months after investment?
options: Not permitted, since all angel investments are locked in for 1 year
Permitted, since the lock-in is 6 months for exit through sale to a third party
Not permitted, since the lock-in is 3 years
Permitted only after SEBI approval
questions.explanation: Angel fund investments are locked in for 1 year; if exit is through sale to a third party (not promoters/associates or buyback), the lock-in is 6 months.
hints: Wrong: the 1-year lock-in is relaxed for third-party sales.
Correct: 6-month lock-in applies for third-party sales.
Wrong: no such lock-in.
Wrong: no SEBI approval needed.
questions.case: Udaan Angel Fund was recently registered with SEBI as an Angel Fund. So far it has on-boarded 4 accredited investors and wants to declare its first close next week. Its manager is evaluating three proposals: (a) investing ₹30 crore in FinBuddy, a fintech start-up; (b) investing ₹2 crore in GreenLeaf, a start-up promoted by a corporate group with group turnover of ₹450 crore; and (c) selling its stake in an existing investee to an unrelated third-party buyer 7 months after the investment was made.

questions.q: Based on the case, the relative (P/E based) value per share of Bharat Foods is:
questions.explanation: EPS = PAT ÷ shares = ₹40 crore ÷ 2 crore = ₹20; price = P/E × EPS = 18 × 20 = ₹360.
hints: Wrong: that is total equity value in crore.
Wrong: arithmetic error.
Wrong: that is EPS.
questions.case: An AIF manager is valuing Bharat Foods Pvt Ltd for a follow-on investment. Bharat Foods has profit after tax of ₹40 crore and 2 crore equity shares outstanding. Comparable listed peers trade at a P/E multiple of 18. The company has debt of ₹200 crore, cash of ₹20 crore and no preference capital; its EBITDA is ₹90 crore. For the DCF cross-check, the risk-free rate is 7%, expected market return is 15% and the company's equity beta is estimated at 1.3.

questions.q: Using the P/E-based equity value, what is Bharat Foods' Enterprise Value?
options: ₹940 crore
₹920 crore
₹540 crore
₹900 crore
questions.explanation: Equity value = ₹360 × 2 crore = ₹720 crore; EV = equity + debt − cash + preference = 720 + 200 − 20 = ₹900 crore.
hints: Wrong: added cash instead of deducting.
Wrong: ignored cash.
Wrong: subtracted debt.
Correct: 720 + 200 − 20 = ₹900 crore.

Comparable listed peers trade at a P/E multiple of 18. The company has debt of ₹200 crore, cash of ₹20 crore and no preference capital; its EBITDA is ₹90 crore. questions.q: What is the implied EV/EBITDA multiple?
hints: Wrong: used equity value (720 ÷ 90).
Wrong: that is the P/E multiple.
Wrong: arithmetic error.

questions.q: Using CAPM, Bharat Foods' cost of equity (before any illiquidity premium) is:
questions.explanation: Ke = Rf + β × (ER − Rf) = 7% + 1.3 × 8% = 17.4%; for an unlisted company an illiquidity premium may be added.
hints: Wrong: that is the market return.
Wrong: omitted the risk-free rate.
